learningObjective: Contrast template-based schedule search (AutoTVM) and template-free schedule search (Ansor / MetaSchedule).

canonicalClaims.claim: Template-based search (AutoTVM) explores parameters of a manually-authored schedule template; template-free search (Ansor / MetaSchedule) generates candidate schedules from the compute definition by composing schedule primitives, eliminating manual template authorship but enlarging the search space.
conditions: The compute definition is expressible in the framework's DSL (TE or TensorIR).
The cost model / evolutionary loop is available to manage the enlarged space.
nonImplications: Does not imply template-free eliminates all human input; compute definitions and cost-model features are still designed.
Does not imply template-free always converges faster.

misconceptions.claim: Template-based search learns the template from data; template-free search enumerates all schedules exhaustively.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AutoTVM templates are human-authored; Ansor uses learned cost models to *prune* the space, not to enumerate exhaustively.

misconceptions.claim: Template-free search always outperforms template-based search.
misconceptions.whyWrong: On well-templated ops with limited tuning budget, template-based can match or beat template-free; the trade-off is engineering effort vs. tuning time.

misconceptions.claim: The two approaches share the same search space; only the measurement backend differs.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The very notion of the space differs: parametrized template vs. free composition of schedule primitives.

misconceptions.claim: Template-free search is fully automatic and requires no domain knowledge.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Domain knowledge shows up in compute definitions, cost-model feature choice, and sketch enumeration rules.

implementationFacts: AutoTVM ships with hand-written templates per operator (e.g., conv2d, matmul).
Ansor uses `sketch` structures that capture algorithmic skeletons and `annotation` phases for parameterization.
MetaSchedule (TVM's successor) uses the same principles applied to TensorIR.
performanceScenarios: For a new operator without an existing template, Ansor can produce a competitive schedule without human template writing.
For a well-templated operator with tight tuning budget, AutoTVM may converge faster.
